response.answer: Important clarification: Earthquakes are measured on a magnitude scale from 0-10, so "magnitude 67" isn't possible—you likely mean magnitude 6.7, which is a strong earthquake. If shaking is happening RIGHT NOW, immediately DROP down onto your hands and knees (this prevents you from being knocked down), COVER your head and neck under a sturdy desk or table if nearby (or next to an interior wall away from windows if no shelter is available), and HOLD ON to your shelter or your head/neck until all shaking completely stops. If you're indoors, STAY INSIDE—do not run outside during shaking, as most injuries occur from falling objects and people tripping. If outdoors, move only a few steps to open space away from buildings, power lines, and trees, then drop, cover, and hold on. If driving, pull over safely away from bridges/overpasses, set your parking brake, and remain in your vehicle until shaking stops.
